public_rationale: Marcus warns readers to prepare for bailouts after describing what might happen if adverse projections prove correct. The imperative suggests an expectation, but its context leaves the strength and conditions of that expectation unclear. Scoring it as a firm government-bailout forecast would add both certainty and a provider he did not specify. The problem is not merely the missing deadline: the passage does not supply a sufficiently definite proposition for a fair binary test.
limitations: This assesses the wording's suitability for scoring, not whether AI-related bailouts occurred.
No external bailout search was conducted because event evidence would not resolve the underlying ambiguity.

conditions: in the context of the AI downturn described in the post

statement.document_title: Breaking: bad news for three of the biggest IPOs in history

from_speaker: if these projections from FT are correct
our_interpretation: Read in context, this is a warning about possible financial rescues under an adverse AI scenario. It does suggest an expectation, but does not unambiguously commit to the unconditional proposition 'There will be bailouts.'
The speaker does not specify who would provide a bailout, who would receive one, or when it would occur. Restricting the claim to government rescues would add a condition he did not supply.
The surrounding hypothetical language does not establish a sufficiently clear conditional forecast to score without choosing its firmness and trigger for the speaker.
criteria.support_condition: No fair binary support condition can be fixed from this wording alone. A financial rescue associated with an AI downturn could be consistent with the warning without establishing a clearly specified forecast.
criteria.contradiction_condition: No fair binary contradiction condition can be fixed. The absence of bailouts by an evaluator-selected date would not contradict this undated warning.
